k.mi: Three slanting strokes stacked: rashers of bacon, a plate of MEAt.
k.mu: A triangle with a gap in its right side: a slice of MOUsse cake, bitten.
k.me: A long slash crossed by a short one: a single stitch to MEnd a tear.
k.mo: Two crossbars on a stem bent right at the base: a MORning scooter.

rules.rule:g: Two small marks at the top right turn a k sound into g: ka becomes ga.
rules.rule:z: Two marks turn an s sound into z: sa becomes za, and shi becomes ji.
rules.rule:d: Two marks turn a t sound into d: ta becomes da. chi and tsu become ji and zu, rarely used; the s-row spellings are normal.
rules.rule:b: Two marks turn an h sound into b: ha becomes ba, fu becomes bu.
rules.rule:p: A small circle at the top right turns an h sound into p: ha becomes pa.
rules.rule:youon: An i-sound kana plus a half-size ya, yu or yo blends into one beat: ki plus small yo is kyo.
rules.rule:ky: ki plus small ya, yu, yo gives kya, kyu, kyo.
rules.rule:sh: shi plus small ya, yu, yo gives sha, shu, sho; the i drops out.
rules.rule:ch: chi plus small ya, yu, yo gives cha, chu, cho.
rules.rule:ny: ni plus small ya, yu, yo gives nya, nyu, nyo.
rules.rule:hy: hi plus small ya, yu, yo gives hya, hyu, hyo.
rules.rule:my: mi plus small ya, yu, yo gives mya, myu, myo.
rules.rule:ry: ri plus small ya, yu, yo gives rya, ryu, ryo, with a light tapped r.
rules.rule:gy: gi plus small ya, yu, yo gives gya, gyu, gyo.
rules.rule:j: ji plus small ya, yu, yo gives ja, ju, jo.
rules.rule:by: bi plus small ya, yu, yo gives bya, byu, byo.
rules.rule:py: pi plus small ya, yu, yo gives pya, pyu, pyo.
rules.rule:extended: Katakana only, for foreign words: a kana plus a half-size vowel makes sounds Japanese lacks.
rules.rule:ti-di-tu: te or de plus small i gives ti, di; to plus small u gives tu.
rules.rule:f: fu plus small a, i, e or o gives fa, fi, fe, fo.
rules.rule:w: u plus small i, e or o gives wi, we, wo, as in loanwords.
rules.rule:she-je-che: shi, ji or chi plus small e gives she, je, che.
rules.rule:v: u with two marks is vu; add small a, i, e or o for va, vi, ve, vo.

pairs.tip: Both: a slash crossed by a big swirl. nu ends in a small closed loop at bottom right; me ends in a plain tail.
All start with an upright and a zigzag swirl. ne ends in a small loop, re ends kicking outward, wa just curls back in.
Same zigzag top and big curve. ru finishes with a small closed loop at the bottom; ro stops open, no loop.
Mirror images. sa's bottom curve bulges left and opens right, like a c; chi's bulges right and opens left, like a 5.
Same slanted stem and bottom curve. ki has two crossbars; sa has only one.
In i the left stroke is the taller one. In ri the right stroke is much longer and swoops down to the left.
ko is just two short stacked strokes. ni is the same pair with a tall upright stroke added on the left.
ha has one crossbar, its stem poking up above it. ho has two bars, and its stem starts at the top bar without poking through.
o has a lone dot at top right, and its stem loops round. a has no dot; a separate stroke loops across its stem.
Both are a top dash over a curve bulging right. u's curve starts flat, running right; ra's starts with a downstroke on the left.
Same tilted cross on the left. ta adds two short stacked strokes; na adds a dot and a stem looping at its foot.
ma: one stem through two bars, poking above the top. ho adds an upright on the left; its stem stops at the top bar.
shi: two flat dashes stacked on the left, long stroke sweeping up. tsu: two steep dashes side by side on top, long stroke falling.
so: steep dash at the top, long stroke falling from top right. n: flatter dash on the left, long stroke sweeping up.
ku's long stroke turns a corner at the top of its tick. ke has a separate flat bar, its stem dropping from the bar's middle.
Both: a long bar and a stem curving left. chi's top is slanted and its stem crosses the bar; te's top is short and flat.
Same shape: a short left post and a roof curving down left. u adds a little tick on top; wa has none.
ko: long top bar, bottom bar stops at the corner. yu: short top, bottom bar runs on past the upright.
fu is a single stroke, a bar then a curve. wa adds a short upright post hanging down from the left end of the bar.
ma: flat bar on top, point at the bottom. mu: point at the top, sitting on a flat base.
ra is fu with a separate short bar floating above it.
no is one lone slanting stroke. me is that same slant crossed by a short stroke running down to the right.
ta is ku with an extra short stroke inside, slanting down right across the middle.
to: one upright, a short stroke jutting right. ho: a full crossbar on top and a short stroke on each side below.
